key_insight: An oxygen pressure of 3.5 bar best balances wear resistance, structural integrity, and frictional stability in HVOF-sprayed Al65Cu20Fe15 coatings.
engineering_relevance: Controlling oxygen pressure can improve coating durability, since lower average friction alone does not guarantee lower wear.
method: Deposit Al65Cu20Fe15 coatings on AISI 321 stainless steel at oxygen pressures of 3.0, 3.5, and 4.0 bar, holding other spray parameters constant.
Characterize microstructure and phase composition using microstructural analysis and X-ray diffraction.
Evaluate dry-sliding friction and wear, coating hardness, and adhesion strength.
evidence_signal: At 3.5 bar, the coating showed the highest quasi-crystalline phase fraction, maximum adhesion, lowest wear rate, and stable friction of 0.55–0.60; all coatings exceeded 750 HV.
watch_item: The 3.5-bar optimum is specific to the tested setup; the abstract does not provide numerical wear rates or test variability to assess transferability.
paper_title: The effect of HVOF spraying parameters on the tribological properties of the Al 65 Cu 20 Fe 15 coatings
